title: Concentrated Gelatinized Proprietary Phenotype Formulation of Lepidium peruvianum (maca) Positively Impacts Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS), Premenstrual Syndrome (PMS), Dysmenorrhea, and Hormone Levels for Fertility Optimization: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS) is considered one of the most common endocrine and metabolic issues in premenopausal (fertile/reproductive age) women. Women with PCOS can experience multiple signs and symptoms, including but not limited to unexplained weight gain or the inability to lose weight, obesity, pelvic pain, virilism, hirsutism, acne, menstrual irregularities, insulin resistance, infertility, decreased follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), increased luteinizing hormone (LH), imbalanced LH/FSH ratio, and increased anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH). Multiple root causes of PCOS have been identified, which may present challenges in determining the best clinical care for women. Further, because the diagnostic criterion for PCOS has changed over time, some confusion within the medical community regarding the best therapies for care exists. Additionally, treatment options can vary based on the criterion each patient meets. It is reported that over two-thirds of women with PCOS are seeking alternative care, such as herbal and supplement options. The purpose of this case report is to share the experience of one woman with PCOS using a concentrated gelatinized proprietary phenotype formulation of Lepidium peruvianum (maca), commercially known as MacaHarmony®, as the primary therapy to address menstrual irregularities, ovulary dysfunction, premenstrual syndrome (PMS), dysmenorrhea, and imbalanced hormones (altered LH/FSH ratio, functionally elevated estradiol, and elevated AMH). In three months, the patient experienced dramatic improvements, including menstrual regularity, enhanced ovulation (improved cervical mucous and libido, decreased ovulatory pain), and decreased length and severity of dysmenorrhea and PMS symptoms (breast tenderness, mood changes). The patient maintained these positive outcomes for over two years. A two-year comparative analysis of labs showed improved LH/FSH ratio and estradiol levels, providing optimized hormonal balance and thereby enhanced fertility potential. In addition, several cardiometabolic markers (glucose, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides) were improved. These improvements may serve as the basis for future research into how specific maca phenotypes or combinations of maca phenotypes, when gelatinized and concentrated, can assist women with PCOS and enhance fertility outcomes.

title: Biociencia y sociología de la educación: el caso de la educación biosocial
abstract: Este artículo argumenta a favor de la educación biosocial como campo de investigación y como marco potencial para la práctica educativa. Se relaciona con los intereses actuales de la sociología de la educación en corporización y afecto, las posibilidades que ofrecen los estudios conceptuales, y los usos de la teoría de recopilación y complejidad para pensar sobre el fenómeno educativo. Además, considera las relaciones más amplias de la teoría de la ciencia social y de la política con la epigenética y la neurociencia. El artículo examina el legado de la biología/sociología y sus riesgos, límites y potencialidades de la investigación biosocial colaborativa, transdisciplinaria y de desplazamiento. El artículo considera los desarrollos en biociencias que puede que tengan resonancia y promesa para la educación, en particular, la epigenética del cuidado y el estrés y la dieta metabolómica. El artículo argumenta que la sociología de la educación debe comprometerse con la biociencia para interrogar los movimientos envolventes de lo social, lo cultural, lo biográfico, lo pedagógico, lo político, lo afectivo, lo neurológico y lo biológico en la producción interactiva de los estudiantes y el aprendizaje.

title: An Examination of the Effect of Parent‐Centered Nutrition Education on the Oxidant‐Antioxidant Parameters of Children Diagnosed With Autism Spectrum Disorder
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study examined the effect of nutrition education given by dietitians to families of children aged 3-18 diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) on meal consumption, eating behaviors, autism severity, serum oxidant/antioxidant marker levels, and total dietary antioxidant capacity. METHODS: The project was carried out with 44 pediatric patients diagnosed with ASD and their parents. The ELISA method was used for antioxidant and oxidant measurements, and the oxygen radical absorbance capacity values ​​of foods defined according to the BeBiS program were used to calculate the total dietary antioxidant capacity. The children's eating behavior questionnaire, childhood autism rating scale (CARS), and brief autism mealtime behavior inventory (BAMBI) were administered. RESULTS: There was no significant difference in antioxidant and oxidant parameters between the experimental and control groups. At the end of eight weeks, superoxide dismutase and glutathione levels increased significantly in the experimental group. There was no significant difference in terms of the families of the autistic children in the experimental and control groups or their disease-specific knowledge. BAMBI scores were similar between the groups at baseline, while a significant decrease was observed in the experimental group at the end of the study. Daily energy, saturated fatty acid (SFA), carbohydrate, and omega-6 intake decreased, while protein, fat, mono- and poly-unsaturated fatty acid, and omega-3 intake increased in the experimental group following nutrition education. However, these results were not statistically significant. There was no significant difference in terms of micronutrient intake between children with ASD in experimental and control groups before and after nutrition education. CONCLUSION: Improvements in eating habits and dietary patterns were noted after nutrition education, especially in the experimental group, even though there were no appreciable changes in oxidative stress indicators. These behavioral shifts imply that family nutrition education can be extremely important in encouraging better eating practices and improving the general well-being of kids with ASD and their families.

title: UNCONJUGATED BILIRUBIN MODULATES THE INTESTINAL EPITHELIAL BARRIER FUNCTION IN A HUMAN‐DERIVED IN VITRO MODEL
abstract: Unconjugated bilirubin promotes intestinal secretion without affecting nutrient digestion or absorption. In the current study, the effects of unconjugated bilirubin on the barrier function of the intestinal epithelium were investigated. Methods: The apical side of human intestinal cell line Caco-2 monolayers was challenged with purified unconjugated bilirubin. Transepithelial electrical resistance and paracellular fluxes of 10kDa Cascade Blue® conjugate dextran were measured. Cell monolayer viability was studied using LDH release and Trypan blue exclusion tests. Redistribution of enterocyte tight junction occludin was studied by confocal microscopy. Bilirubin induced a dose-dependent decrease of transepithelial electrical resistance. This effect was maximal at 6 hours and tended to be reversed at 48 hours. Oxidated bilirubin was ineffective. Bilirubin significantly increased fluorescent dextran paracellular passage. Cell viability was not affected by unconjugated bilirubin over the 5-200nM, concentration range. Finally, bilirubin triggered a reversible redistribution of tight junctional occludin. Unconjugated bilirubin increases the permeability of intestinal epithelium. This effect is reversible, dependent on the redox status of the molecule and on the rearrangement of the tight junction. Conclusion: These data attribute to bilirubin a novel role of functional modulator of intestinal paracellular permeability in vitro. We are currently investigating the intracellular cascade triggered by bilirubin.

title: THE AETIOLOGY AND MANAGEMENT OF EXTRA HEPATIC PORTAL VEIN OBSTRUCTION IN CHILDREN: A SINGLE CENTRE EXPERIENCE
abstract: To study predisposing factors, presenting features, management and long-term outcome of extra hepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO). The medical records of 108 children (67 male, median age 4.75 [range 1 day-16.3] years) with EHPVO between Jan 1979 and Sept 2005 were reviewed retrospectively. Median follow up period was 6 [range 0.39-19.5] years. Clinical, haematological and biochemical features on presentation, management of bleeding and long term outcome were recorded. Predisposing factors like umbilical line catheterization, peritoneal sepsis were identified in 14 (13%) and 9 (8%). Detailed investigations into procoagulant states were available in 30 patients: protein C was low in 6, protein S was slightly low in 2 and factor V Leiden heterozygosity was seen in 1. Clinical presentation included splenomegaly in 91%, ascites in 4%. Abnormal liver enzymes and INR were seen in 13 and 14 children respectively. Haematological parameters of hypersplenism were present in 13 (12%). Bleeding occurred in 83 (77%) patients, for whom it was the presenting feature in 78 (94%). Median age at first bleeding was 4.58 years [range 0.02-16.37]. On first endoscopy oesophageal varices were present in 92 (93%) patients, 70 (76%) received sclerotherapy, 5 (5%) were banded and 16 (17%) both. Six [1-20] sclerotherapy or 2 [1-5] banding sessions were required to eradicate the varices. Complications of endoscopy occurred in 34 (37%) patients: esophageal ulcers in 16, esophageal stricture in 10, ulcers and strictures in 7 and erosive gastritis in 1. 17 (16%) children underwent shunt surgery for uncontrolled bleeding at a median age of 9.7 [range, 5.2-23.7] and the shunt is functioning in 8 patients at a follow up of 12.8 [2.3-19.5] years. All those with non-functioning shunts had gastrointestinal bleeding which was controlled with sclerotherapy in 7. One required liver transplantation and one had a second shunt operation which was successful. The aetiology of EHPVO in most children remains unknown. Sclerotherapy and banding are an effective treatment for bleeding varices with good long term outcome.

title: PORTAL GASTROPATHY AND DUODENOPATHY IN CHILDREN WITH EXTRAHEPATIC VERSUS INTRAHEPATIC PORTAL HYPERTENSION: ENDOSCOPICAL DIAGNOSIS AND HISTOLOGICAL SCORING
abstract: Portal gastropathy (PG) and duodenopathy (PD) can cause life threatening bleeding in children with portal hypertension (PH). However, pediatric data on the frequency of these gastroduodenal lesions is scarce and there is no widely accepted criteria for the diagnosis of gastroduodenal pathologies associated with PH in the pediatric age group other than the varices. We aimed to determine the frequency and demographical characteristics of portal hypertensive gastroduodenal lesions, compare the endoscopical markers with different histological findings and evaluate the use of a possible histological scoring system. Thirtythree consecutive children (16 males, mean age 9.9 ± 4.5 yrs, range 0.5-18 yrs) undergoing endoscopical investigation for PH were analysed. Clinical and demographical data, endoscopical and histological findings as well as the presence of H. pylori infection were recorded. Endoscopical portal hypertensive mucosal lesions were scored according to the Baveno classification. Histological findings suggestive of PH (capillary dilatation, increased numbers of capillaries, histological bleeding and edema) were scored and portal hypertensive gastropathy and duodenopathy scores were calculated. Results were comparatively analysed for different etiological groups. Sixteen children were noncirrhotic. PG was diagnosed in 33.3 % endoscopically. Children with noncirrhotic intrahepatic (IH) PH had the lowest rate of PG (11.1 %) whereas those with extrahepatic (EH) PH or cirrhosis were quite alike (42.9 % and 41.2 % respectively). PELD score correlated with PG in cirrhotics. Edema was the only histological finding showing significant association with the endoscopical diagnosis (p < 0.01). Total PG score calculated by adding scores for each histological finding did not prove superior. Only 6.1 % had PD on endoscopy. Again histological findings other than edema poorly correlated with an endoscopical diagnosis of PD. Demographical, clinical, endoscopical and histological findings of 33 portal hypertensive children have been analysed and the possible use of a histological scoring system has been evaluated in this study. PG is less frequently observed in noncirrhotic IHPH and strongly correlates with severity of liver disease in cirrhotics. Histological edema is the best histological indicator of PG. Addition of other findings doesn't improve diagnosis.

title: GROWTH AND INTESTINAL FUNCTION 3 TO 16 YEARS AFTER INTESTINAL TRANSPLANTATION
abstract: To study the absorptive function of the transplanted intestine on the long term. from 1994, among 65 transplanted children, 24 (5 girls) were followed more than 2 years with a functional graft. A girl transplanted in 1989 is also included. The graft is an isolated intestine (7), plus the liver (18), plus the colon (12). Median follow-up is 6 years (2-16). Treatment is tacrolimus and prednisone (<0.2 mg/kg) on alternate days. Serum markers of malnutrition, stool components and biopsies were controlled. all patients were weaned from parenteral nutrition. PN was re-instituted in 2, 8 y post-transplantation for chronic rejection (non compliance), and 6 y post-transplantation for a fistula secondary to surgery for occlusion. The mean caloric intake is 20% more than recommended for age. Enteral nutrition is needed in 13/25 at 2 y, 5/18 at 5 y (2 severe anorexia). Three still have an ileostomy. Growth velocity is normal, 8/25 have a growth curve <− 2 SD for height, 3/4 adults have a normal final height. Weight is normal for height. The global and fat absorption rates are 88/80 % at 2y, 86/76 % at 5 y, 84/68 % at 7 y (only 3 patients). Pancreatic function is normal. Pancreatic enzyme supplementation does not modify the growth velocity. Cholesterol is low (3.1 mM), vitamins ADE are normal with supplements, coagulation is normal. In biopsies, intestinal villi are normal. Inflammation is moderate to important in 3/9 2 y, 3/5 7 y, 2/3 10 y, 0/1 15 y post-transplantation., predominating in the colon. the absorptive function is adequate to support growth. Steatorrhea may be due to persistent lymphangiectasia. Final height will probably be normal, with a high caloric intake and delayed puberty. Late graft loss is rare. Inflammation should be followed (chronic rejection ? risk of cancer ?). the functional results of intestinal transplantation are satisfactory on the mid-and long-term.

title: EFFECT OF EXCLUSIVE ENTERAL NUTRITION ON BONE METABOLISM IN CHILDREN WITH CROHN'S DISEASE
abstract: Crohn's Disease (CD), a chronic inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract, may also impact upon a number of extra-intestinal sites, including bone. This study aims to investigate the complex interactions between gut inflammation and bone metabolism and to further develop evidence for the numerous benefits of exclusive enteral feeding in children with CD. 17 children with newly diagnosed CD were treated with polymeric formula for 8 weeks, provided as per standard protocol. Weight, height and serum samples were collected prior to and upon ceasing the exclusive enteral feeding regimen. Inflammatory markers (CRP, albumin) were measured; disease activity was assessed by the pediatric Crohn's disease activity index (PCDAI) and serum CrossLaps (CTx), a marker of bone resorption was measured by ELISA. At diagnosis children with CD had below average mean weight Z scores for chronological age. PCDAI, CRP and CTx were raised and albumin was reduced. Mean weight Z scores improved after enteral feeding (p=0.001), but height Z scores were unchanged. Disease activity scores fell and albumin levels increased with enteral feeding (p=0.0141), but CRP levels did not significantly improve. Mean CTx was reduced with exclusive enteral feeding from 2.213ng/ml to 1.629ng/ml (p=<0.0001). In addition to improving nutritional status and inducing disease remission, exclusive enteral feeding decreased bone resorption in this group of children. Although analysis of markers of bone formation is required to complement these findings, there is clear evidence that exclusive enteral feeding reduces bone resorption. These results further support the role of exclusive enteral feeding as primary therapy in paediatric CD.

title: PROMOTER ANALYSIS SUGGESTS THE IMPLICATION OF NF100001KAPPAB/C‐REL TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS IN BILIARY ATRESIA
abstract: Microarray studies used to describe altered gene expression patterns in tissues provide a promising new way to provide insight into the pathomechanism of biliary atresia (BA). Our hypothesis was that altered gene expression in BA may be linked to regulatory transcription factors (TF). The overrepresentation of transcription factor binding sites (TFBS) in the promoter regions of genes with altered expression would support this hypothesis. Using data published in three papers we analyzed the prevalence of TFBSs in the promoter regions of genes with altered expression in BA and compared it with the overall prevalence in known promoter sequences. title: MODULATION OF FATTY ACID COMPOSITION OF LUNG TISSUES OF MICE CHRONICALLY INFECTED WITH PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA (PA): THE FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCES
abstract: Cystic fibrosis is characterized by a high susceptibility to lung infection by Pa. We used an omega 3 fatty acid diet to enhance host defense through anti-inflammatory properties. 1) to investigate the effects of the dietary intake of ω 6 or ω 3 fatty acids (FA) on the FA composition of tissue phospholipids (phosphatidylcholine PC and -ethanolamine PE) in lung of chronically infected mice, 2) to evaluate the functional consequences in these animals. The infection was performed on C57BL/6 mice, 5 weeks old, after 5 weeks of nutrition with 3 diets with high contents of either omega 3 (EPA C20:5 w3, diet A), or omega 6 PUFA (AA C20:4 w6, diet B), compared to a control diet. Animals were infected intratracheally with Pa (PAO1 strain) included in agarose beads. Six mice of each group were sacrificed at day 1, day 4 and day 7 seven after infection. Lung samples were immediately frozen for further determinations. Tissues phospholipids were fractionated by HPTLC and fatty acid profile of PC and PE were determined by gas chromatography. Distal fluid clearance was evaluated as well as mortality in these animals. EPA was significantly increased (p < 0.0001) in PC and PE fractions of lung phospholipids of mice placed on diet A (PE: 4+/−1, PC: 1.9+/−0.6) as compared to mice placed on diet B (PE: 0.7+/−0.1, PC: 0.2 ± 0.1) or placed on the control diet (PE: 0.1 ± 0.1, PC: 0.1 ± 0.1). title: PPAR‐GAMMA2 PRO12ALA VARIANT, INSULIN RESISTANCE AND LCPUFA IN OBESE CHILDREN
abstract: To examine whether an association of PPAR-γ2 Pro12Ala with insulin resistance and LCPUFA may exist in obese children. One-hundred and forty obese children (58 girls and 82 boys, mean age [SD], 10.2 [2.7] y) entered this observational study. Obesity was defined in accordance with the International Obesity Task Force. Body mass index (BMI) z scores were calculated and adjusted by using the Cole-s LMS-method. Fasting blood samples were taken for measurements of glucose, insulin levels, lipid profile, and plasma fatty acids (FA) composition (expressed as % total FA). Insulin resistance (IR) was estimated by the homeostatic model assessment (HOMA-IR). Genomic DNA was obtained from peripheral blood using standard methods, and the Pro12Ala PPAR-γ2 variant was detected by DNA sequencing. Dietary habits of children were assessed at recruitment by means of an age-adjusted Food Frequency Questionnaire. Statistics: Mann-Whitney test and linear regression. Significance was further adjusted for gender, afe, Tanner stage and BMI z-score. Prevalence of Ala carriers was 18.6%. Compared to Pro/Pro, Pro12Ala genotype was associated with lower values of fasting insulin levels (p=0.017), HOMA-IR (p=0.022), plasma levels of C20:3n-9 (p=0.047) and n-6/n-3 LCPUFA in plasma phosholipids (p=0.019) and higher levels of arachidonic (AA) (p<0.01), eicosapentaenoic (EPA) (p=0.03) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) (p=0.041) in plasma phosholipids. title: BONE MARROW TRANSPLANTATION IN CHILDREN WITH SEVERE INFLAMMATORY INTESTINAL DISEASES
abstract: We report here the six cases of children with intractable inflammatory bowel disease who were refractory to usual immunosuppressive treatments but responded to allogenic bone marrow transplantation (BMT). The six cases consisted of two brothers with intractable ulcerating enterocolitis (IE) of infancy, three brothers had X-linked lymphoproliferative disease (XLP) and a boy with severe inflammatory disease affecting skin and gut. Three brothers diagnosed with deletion of the SAP gene (SH2D1A) causative for XLP aged 13, 12, and 9 yrs initially presented with recurrent infections with low immunoglobulin levels requiring replacement therapy. One of these brothers had had previously a high grade abdominal B-NHL. All had an unusual chronic gastritis and pan-colitis with mucosal lymphocytic and eosinophilic infiltrates. Two brothers presented with IE. The sixth patient, a 10-year old boy, had presented with a severe erythrodermatous skin, refractory to immunosupressor associated with an autoimmune enterocolitis. 5/6 patients underwent allogenic BMT bone marrow transplantation (BMT) with rapid engraftement, and the 10-year old boy underwent a cord blood transplantation. Following the BMT, five of the six children had shown symptoms of graft versus host disease (GVHD) affecting the gut, the skin, and/or the liver. Some had bacterial, viral (EBV, astrovirus, adenovirus) or fungal infections linked to the BMT immunosuppressive treatment. Intestinal histology, when performed, only showed signs of GVHD. Inflammatory diseases affecting skin and gut are usually associated with an underlying systemic immunodysregulation and may prove refractory to conventional immunosuppressive treatment such as azathioprine, cyclosporin, tacrolimus and monoclonal antibodies. BMT is an efficacious treatment in this group of patients.

title: CONDITIONAL INACTIVATION OF IKBA IN INTESTINAL EPITHELIAL CELLS INDUCES DEVELOPMENT FO SECONDARY LYMPHOID ORGANS
abstract: The epithelial cell layer in the gut has a key role in the regulation of the innate immune system. Most importantly these epithelial cells participate in the discrimination between pathogens and non pathogens. Proinflammatory cytokines and pathogens induce expression and secretion of cytokines and chemokines in epitheila cells. The majority of these inflammatory molecules are targets of NF-κB/Rel/IκB and controlled by the IκB kinase pathway. Since most of the available data are generated in in vitro model, we aimed to define the role of NF-κB/Rel/IκB in epithelial cells of the gut in vivo in the mouse. MIP3α and BLC are expressed in the areas of infiltrations in the colon. Interestingly, both component of the alternative NF-κB pathway (NF-κB2, RelB) are induced in IκBα deficient epithelial cells. IκBα in epithelial cells of the gut regulated development of lymphoid organs in the intestine.

title: GOS & FOS PLAY A PROTECTIVE ROLE VS NEONATAL JAUNDICE
abstract: To examine whether supplementing formula with oligosaccharide mixture may modulate bilirubin total (BT) levels in formula fed infants during the first weeks of life by modification of intestinal microflora. Fifty healthy full-term infants were double blind randomly allocated into two groups to receive either supplementation of oligosacharides mixture producted by Numico Research (GOS/FOS ratio 9:1) at the dosage of 0.8 g/100ml (n = 27) or placebo (maltodexrine) (n = 23), from birth through the first 28 days of life. BT (TcB) level was determined by multiwavelength spectral analysis, (BiliCheck device SpectRx Inc Norcross, GA) within 2 hours after birth (T0), at 24, 48, 72 h and at completed 5, 7, 10, 28 (T8) days of life. Capillary hematocrit (HT) was further determined by conventional methods. Groups were comparable for birth weight, gestational age, maternal age, type of delivery, baseline (T0) serum* TcB level (mean [SD; range], gos-fos 3.0 [0.7; 2.1-4.8] vs. placebo 3.0 [0.8; 1.6-5.0] mg/dl, and HT level. Pattern of TcB significantly differed between groups through the study (P < 0.01; Anova for repeated measures). Infants in supplemented group exhibited lower plasma TcB levels than placebo group from 72 h of life onwards (P < 0.02). At T8, mean [SD; range] TcB level was 2.4 [0.5; 1.1-3.6] mg/dl (gos-fos) vs. 2.8 [0.4; 1.8-3.8] mg/dl (placebo). HT significantly decreased from birth to day 28 in both groups (P < 0.0001) but no difference between groups was found (P > 0.55). In formula fed infants, supplementation of a mixture of gos-fos significantly lowers bilirubin level after 72 hours of life. It may be hypothesize that stimulating the intestinal growth of bifidobacteria and lactobacilli enhances bilirubin excretion by reducing it to urobilinoids. Larger randomized trials would be of interest to evaluate prophylactic and therapeutic use of gos-fos in neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia.

title: FOCAL VILLOUS ATROPHY OF THE DUODENUM IN CHILDREN WHO HAVE OUTGROWN COW'S MILK ALLERGY H BIOACTIVE MILK FAT GLOBULE MEMBRANE PROTEINS ‐ CHROMOENDOSCOPY AND MAGNIFICATION ENDOSCOPY EVALUATION
abstract: Patchy villous atrophy of duodenal mucosa has been described in young children with cows's milk allergy (CMA). Cows's milk protein-sensitive enteropathy may persist in older children and shows characteristic histological features. The advent of magnification endoscopy may allow the macroscopic detection of unrecognized villous atrophy in these patients. The aim of the study was to evaluate the duodenum mucosa in older children with cow's milk allergy in infancy using chromoendoscopy and magnification endoscopy. The study involved 15 children (9 girls; mean aged 15 years; range 12-18) with CMA diagnosed and treated in infancy, currently on normal diet, referred to our department due to abdominal pain. The control group consisted of 8 children with abdominal pain without any evidence of allergy (5 girls, mean age 15 years, range 13-18). In all patients the chromoendoscopy was performed with a magnification endoscope (GIFQ 160Z, Olympus) and videotaped for detailed analysis. For staining 1% solution of methylene blue was sprayed over the mucosa. All examination were conducted under general anesthesia. The bulb and the descending portion of the duodenum was examined. Pathological findings were defined as focal villous atrophy. Seven of 15 patients (47%) with CMA in infancy had focal villous atrophy of the descending part of the duodenum. In 1 patient erosions of bulb were present. In the control group, the villous atrophy was seen in 1 case (12.5%). This is the first study demonstrating by magnification endoscopy that in children who have outgrown cow's milk allergy the patchy villous atrophy of the duodenum is a common finding. Magnification endoscopy may be useful for detecting mucosal abnormalitis, delineating there extent, and allowing target.

title: THE PROBIOTIC E. COLI NISSLE 1917 TRAINS PROTECTING AGAINST MURINE ACUTE COLITISTY AND NEW WAYS FOR PREVENTION OF INFECTIONS ‐ AN EFFECTIVE THERAPY OPTION IN CHILDREN WITH UNSPECIFIC PROLONGED DIARRHOEA
abstract: Infants and toddlers with prolonged diarrhoea over several days are in danger of developing dehydration and an acute deterioration of their general state of health. So far no effective causal therapy exists. Therefore in a confirmatory, randomized, double-blind clinical trial the efficacy of the probiotic bacterial strain E. coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) as compared to a placebo was tested. In total, 151 children aged 1 month to 47 months (Ø 25 months) with unspecific prolonged diarrhoea (> 3 watery or loose stools without blood in 24 hours of a diarrhoeal episode, which has been persisting for more than 4 consecutive days but not longer than 14 days) were randomized in a double-blind design to receive either the probiotic EcN suspension (n = 75) or placebo (n = 76). All children were dehydrated to a medium extent (5 - 10% loss of body weight) and received 1 to 3 ml verum or placebo suspension orally per day depending on the age (1 ml suspension contained 108 viable EcN bacteria) for 21 days. At study commencement, rehydration (ORL according to WHO) was performed once. The number of patients showing a reduction of stool frequency to less than 3 watery or loose stools in 24 hours over a period of at least 4 consecutive days (response rate) was higher in the EcN group than in the placebo group already on day 7 (EcN 78.7%, placebo 59.2%) The response rate increased continuously as was measured on days 14 (EcN 93.3%, placebo 65.8%) and 21 (EcN 98.7%, placebo 71.1%). The two-sample test of rates following a group sequential test design showed statistically significant superiority for EcN on both days 14 (p = 0.0017) and 21 (p < 0.0001). Due to its excellent efficacy the probiotic EcN is a suitable remedy in treatment of prolonged diarrhoea. Using the probiotic EcN prolonged diarrhoea can be successfully treated.

title: IRON NUTRITION AMONG ONE YEAR OLD HEALTHY CHILDREN IN SWEDEN
abstract: To describe possible social and nutritional factors influencing iron status and iron intake among healthy one year old children in Sweden. Parents to 12 months old children (n=90) answered a questionnaire concerning the child's feeding during the first year. Demographical data were obtained. The total food intakes at 12 months were recorded for five days. Blood samples for analyses of haemoglobin (Hb), mean corpuscular volume (MCV), S-ferritin and transferrin receptor (TfR) were obtained. Partially breastfeeding at 12 months were received by 19,6 % of the children and correlated negatively with the iron intake. Children whose mothers reported an educational level < 9 years had significantly lower iron intake (p=0,003), lower Hb (p=0,04) and lower MCV (p= 0,009) compared to the children whose mothers reported a higher level of education. Twenty five percent of the parents reported feeding difficulties when the child was 12 months and these children had significantly lower weight at 12 months (p=0,003) compared to those children whose parents did not report feeding difficulties. Thirty four percent of the parents had received information about iron rich food from the Child Health Services and there were significantly lower values of TfR (p=0,01) among the children whose parents received information about iron rich food compared to those children whose parents had not received information. Thirty percent of the children had an iron intake below the Nordic Nutrition recommendations of 8 mg/day. Follow-on formula and iron fortified porridge contributed to 64 % of the total iron intake. In total, 10 % of the children were found to be iron depleted (S-ferritin < 12 μg/L) and 2,2 % had iron deficiency with or without anaemia (haemoglobin ≤ 100 g/L). This study showed that partially breastfeeding and low maternal education correlated negatively with the iron intake. Iron fortified products contributed with a large proportion of the iron intake. Many children did not reach the recommended iron intake. Information about food with high content of iron resulted in improved iron status.

title: OXIDATIVE LIVER INJURY IN RATS DUE TO ISONIAZID AND THE DECREASE OF THIS OXIDATIVE STRESS BY USING VITAMIN C
abstract: To study the effects of isoniazid (INH) in combination with vitamin C on blood and tissue levels of oxidative / antioxidative parameters and biochemical markers. Forty rats were divided into 4 groups: 1) control group; 2) INH (50 mg/kg/day) was given; 3) INH + low dose vitamin C (100 mg/kg/day) were given; 4) INH + high dose vitamin C (1000 mg/kg/day) were given for a period of 21 days. After 3 weeks, the rats were sacrificed after ketamin anesthesia and liver and blood samples were obtained. Serum levels of AST, ALT, GGT, ALP, total cholesterol, and triglycerides were studied in all. Oxidant and antioxidant parameters [malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione peroxidase (GSH-px), glutathione (GSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and vitamin C] levels were studied in both serum and liver samples. In INH-given group, serum level of MDA, AST, ALT, and GGT were higher, but both serum and liver tissue levels of antioxidant parameters, GSH-px and GSH were lower when compared to the control group (p< 0.005). On the other hand, when compared to INH-given group, MDA, AST, ALT, and GGT levels were lower and GSH-px and GSH levels were higher in rats given INH + low dose vitamin C (p<0.005). These results were comparable with those of the control group. When vitamin C is given in high doses, while liver enzymes, serum and liver MDA levels were improved like in the case of low dose administration, erythrocyte and liver tissue GSH levels were lower than those in control group. Increased oxidative stress play a role in the development of liver injury induced by INH. Vitamin C, being a potent scavenger of toxic free radicals and other reactive oxygen species, may improve this situation with a low dose such as 100 mg/kg/day. Our experimental study suggested that low dose vitamin C may attenuate liver injury induced by INH use. High dose vitamin C is not more potent antioxidant compared to low dose. Even it may act as a pro-oxidant by decreasing blood and liver GSH levels.

title: CHOLESTASIS SYNDROME IN CHILDREN WITH KAWASAKI DISEASE
abstract: Kawasaki disease and cholestasis syndrome are rare in children. The aim of the study was to search for cholestasis syndrome in Kawasaki disease. We retrospectively reviewed medical records of patients admitted to tertiary University Hospital during 1998-2004 yrs. Medical records of all patients with Kawasaki disease were reviewed. We found 21 patients with Kawasaki disease. Four of them had Kawasaki disease with cholestasis syndrome. The data of these patients are presented in the table. Itching started from the first days of the disease and prolonged for 1-4wk. The course of the disease was benign in all patients nevertheless they were treated or not with i/v imunoglobulin. Cholestasis syndrome is not a rare entity in Kawasaki disease. Pronounced intching from the beginning of the disease could be the first symtom of cholestasis syndrome.

title: THE EFFECT OF REPEATED DOSES OF ESOMEPRAZOLE ON PHARMACODYNAMIC AND PHARMACOKINETIC VARIABLES IN INFANTS AGED 1 TO 24 MONTHS WITH GERD
abstract: To measure the effects of repeated doses of esomeprazole on the pharmacokinetics (PK), intragastric pH, intraesophageal pH and reflux episodes in patients, aged 1-24 months, with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) symptoms. In this single-centre, randomised, single-blind study (SH-NEC-0001) infants with symptoms of GERD (irritability/crying, vomiting, choking/gagging) and ≥5% time with intraesophageal pH < 4 received oral esomeprazole 0.25mg/kg or 1mg/kg for 8 days. On day 7 or 8 blood samples (0.6ml) were taken for PK analysis and 24-hour esophageal and gastric pH were measured. 50 infants were randomised to treatment. The mean percentage of time with intragastric pH > 4 at baseline was 30.5% and 28.6% in the esomeprazole 0.25mg/kg and 1mg/kg groups, respectively. After treatment, the mean percentage of time with intragastric pH > 4 was significantly higher with esomeprazole 1mg/kg (69.3%) than with esomeprazole 0.25mg/kg (47.9%) (p < 0.001). The mean percentage of time with intraesophageal pH < 4 at baseline was 11.6% and 12.5% in the esomeprazole 0.25mg/kg and 1mg/kg groups, respectively. Both esomeprazole dosages decreased the percentage of time with intraesophageal pH < 4, to means of 8.4% and 5.5%, respectively. On day 7/8, the number of reflux episodes longer than 5 minutes decreased from a mean of 6 at baseline to 3 and 2 with esomeprazole 0.25mg/kg and 1mg/kg, respectively. For both dosages there was large inter-individual variability in the PK variables. Numerically there was a larger-than-dose proportional increase in AUC, AUCtao and steady state maximum concentration (CSSmax) between dosages, although this was not statistically significant. Both dosages of esomeprazole were well-tolerated. Repeated administration of 0.25mg/kg and 1mg/kg of esomeprazole resulted in a dose-related increase in the percentage of time with intragastric pH > 4, and a reduction in the percentage of time with intraesophageal pH < 4, in infants aged 1-24 months with GERD.

title: THE NATURAL HISTORY OF COW'S MILK PROTEIN SENSITISATION IN INFANTILE ALLERGIC COLITIS CONSTIPATION‐ AN ASSOCIATION WITH MULTIPLE FOOD ALLERGY?
abstract: To document the clinical outcome and evidence of persisting dietary sensitisation, in particular, cow's milk protein (CMP), in infants with allergic colitis (AC). We carried out a prospective study with comprehensive evaluation of immunological (1), endoscopic, clinical profiles and follow up for assessment of in vivo/in vitro evidence of CMP sensitivity. 12 AC infants were diagnosed, median onset at 6 weeks (2 days-7 months). Clinical cow's milk sensitivity was defined by resolution of bloody diarrhoea on CMP exclusion (with maternal dairy exclusion or amino acid formula) and subsequent rechallenge (open in breast fed, double blind challenge in amino acid formula fed). Clinical reactions to sequential dietary antigen introduction during weaning (soya/wheat/egg etc.) were documented. 10/12 had CMP sensitivity, 5/10 showed positive Th1/Th2 blood mononuclear responses (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-5 cytokine production by ELISPOT to casein and/or beta-lactoglobulin), 3 with Th2 lamina propria CMP responses. 9/10 CMP sensitive AC infants were followed up to median 23 months (8-34 months). One infant was lost to follow-up before CMP rechallenge. CMP was tolerated in 3 cases by 12 months, 1 case by 18 months and 2 cases by 24 months. 3 cases were still CMP sensitive at 21, 23 and 34 months. Multiple food allergy (≥2 antigens) with positive gastrointestinal reactions and/or cutaneous manifestations, both immediate and delayed onset, were observed in 6 CMP sensitive cases (soya, n = 5; eggs, n = 3; others, n = 2; none to wheat). Unrestricted diet was achieved in just 4/8 CMP sensitive AC infants in the follow-up period. In this group of AC with early CMP sensitisation, the clinical resolution and dietary tolerance were variable and often delayed. Although this may reflect a selective populaton, it highlights the importance of longer term dietary follow-up despite CMP tolerance by age one year.

title: DOCOSAHEXAENOIC ACID STATUS OF BREASTFED INFANTS CAN BE IMPROVED BY LOW DOSE SUPPLEMENTATION OF THEIR MOTHERS DURING PREGNANCY AND LACTATION
abstract: The aim was to investigate the effect of a low dose of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, 22:6 n-3) in a daily supplement for pregnant and lactating mothers on the DHA concentration in breast milk, and in red blood cell (RBC) phospholipids of their infants. At 22 weeks of pregnancy, 144 mothers were enrolled to a randomized controlled double blind clinical trial on the daily intake of one of three supplements up to 37 weeks, and voluntarily up to 3 months after delivery. The first supplement contained minerals, and vitamins (Min/Vit), the second additionally contained a prebiotic (Prebio), and the third additionally 0.2 g DHA from fish oil (LCPUFA). Questionnaires and product consumption measurements verified compliance. At 3 months, samples of milk were obtained from 58 mothers, and of venous blood from 33 infants. The samples were stored in ice and shipped immediately to be frozen at 70°C under nitrogen until analysed by gas-liquid chromatography. Treatment differences were estimated in the intention to treat (ITT) and per protocol (PP) data set by ANCOVA, correcting for the baseline measurement of the mother at week 22 (p-values adjusted for multiple tests). The DHA concentration (% of total fatty acids) at 3 months in breastmilk in the ITT data set was 0.25 (+/− 0.10) compared to 0.26 (+/−0.13), and to 0.50 (+/−0.19) in the Min/Vit-, Prebio-, and LCPUFA- group, respectively. The treatment effect was significant in the LCPUFA-group compared to the Min/Vit- and to the Prebio-group utilizing the ITT data set, as well as the PP data set (p=0.0000 and 0.0000, resp.). The RBC- DHA concentration (% of total fatty acids) at 3 months in infants in the ITT data set was 7.49 (+/− 2.00) compared to 6.88 (+/−2.76), and to 9.79 (+/−2.21) in the Min/Vit-, Prebio-, and LCPUFA-group, respectively. Again, the treatment effects were significantly different in the groups of the ITT-data set, and still recognizable in the PP data set. There was a significant correlation between DHA concentrations in breastmilk, and in infant RBC in the ITT and PP data set (p=0.02). The same effects could be observed for eicosapentaenoic acid, but no statistical difference between groups was found for arachidonic acid. Maternal low dose DHA-supplements in pregnancy and lactation influenced the DHA-concentration in the lipids of breastmilk and the infants' RBC. To improve the DHA status of the infant, supplements for pregnant and lactating mothers should contain DHA

title: CLINICAL FEATURES AND EFFECT OF PRIMARY BILE ACIDS IN CHILDREN WITH 3‐BETA‐HYDROXY‐D5‐C27‐STEROID DEHYDROGENASE/ISOMERASE DEFICIENCY DIAGNOSED AT DIFFERENT AGES
abstract: 3β-hydroxy-D5-C27-steroid dehydrogenase/isomerase (3β-HSD) deficiency causes severe cholestasis and chronic liver disease. Prompt identification and treatment avoid the progression of the disease. We aimed to define its natural history and response to treatment at different ages. Four patients diagnosed by tandem mass spectrometry and monitored by liver function tests (LFTs) and urinary 3β,7α dihydroxy-5-cholenoic acid (3β,7α DH5C) that was increased in all at diagnosis. GGT was normal in all. Patient 1 was initially started on ursodehoxycholic acid (UDCA) for 2.5 years. All 4, upon diagnosis, received 10 mg/kg/day of a combination of UDCA and chenodehoxycholic acid (CDCA). Patient 1 presented at 2.5 months of age with giant cell hepatitis, was initially misdiagnosed and started on UDCA with prompt normalisation of liver function tests (LFTs). At 2.5 years of age, the time of diagnosis, a second liver biopsy showed worsened fibrosis. Following the start of CDCA urinary 3β,7α DH5C normalised, and a further follow up biopsy showed no progression of fibrosis. Patient 2 (sibling of pt 1) was diagnosed at birth. LFTs were normal. The child, started on UDCA and CDCA, normalised 3β,7α DH5C levels and has minimal inflammation at liver biopsy at the age of 4 years. Patient 3 had a history of jaundice, hepatomegaly, bleeding during her stay in Morocco. She presented at 7 years of age with INR 1.4, normal bilirubin, and ALT, low GGT, and had biopsy proven cirrhosis. Following treatment 3β,7α DH5C normalised. Patient 4 (sibling of pt 3) presented with failure to thrive, jaundice with acholic stools, hepato-splenomegaly, severe coagulopathy (INR 2.3), ALT 329 U/l, GGT 30 and biopsy proven cirrhosis. After treatment he cleared jaundice, INR is 1.4, ALT 57; 3β,7α DH5C disappeared. β-hydroxy-D5-C27-steroid dehydrogenase/isomerase should be suspected at any paediatric age in patients with chronic liver disease and low GGT, whatever the severity of cholestasis and coagulopathy. Treatment with CDCA corrects the defect improving and stabilising liver disease.

title: OCCURRENCE OF TYPE 1 DIABETES TOGETHER WITH CELIAC DISEASE IS NOT ASSOCIATED WITH MBL DEFICIENCY
abstract: Mannan-binding lectin (MBL) is a pattern recognition molecule involved in the innate immune system, able to differentiate between the carbohydrates found on self glycoproteins and the carbohydrate patterns found on infectious non-self surfaces. MBL deficiency seems to increase the susceptibility to chronic inflammation and certain autoimmune diseases and an increased frequency has been reported in celiac disease (CD).. We tested the hypothesis that MBL deficiency is associated with the development of Type 1 diabetes (T1D) in patients with CD. A population sample of a total of 79 patients (all HLA-DQ2 and/or HLA-DQ8) of Caucasian ethnicity (1-15 years of age) with CD of whom 41 had associated T1D and an age-matched control group of children with T1D (n=48) were investigated. Polymorphisms in exon 1 of the MBL-2 gene were detected by direct sequencing using ABI PRISM BigDye Terminator v3.1 Cycle Sequencing Kit (Applied Biosystems) and an ABI Prism 3100 Genetic Analyzer (Applied Biosystems). There were no differences in the frequency of structural mutation homozygotes or compound heterozygotes (O/O) between CD patients (n = 38) and CD patients with associated T1D (n = 41) (P = 0.91; Odds Ratio: 0.92 (95% CI: 0.21-3.97)). The frequency of O/O in all CD patients (CD and CD with associated T1D combined; n = 79) was approximately twice as high as the frequency in patients with T1D alone (n = 48) (0.10 and 0.04, respectively). This difference was not significant (P = 0.22; Odds Ratio: 2.59 (95% CI: 0.53-12.75)). Examination of the three mutant alleles of the MBL gene causing MBL deficiency in patients with CD and CD patients with associated T1D revealed that MBL deficiency is not a risk factor for the occurrence of T1D in CD patients.

title: INSULIN SECRETION IN CHILDREN ON LONG‐TERM PARENTERAL NUTRITION
abstract: In children on long-term cyclic parenteral nutrition (LTPN), chronic hyperinsulinaemia due high rates of nutrient delivery, the possible toxicity of lipids and the decrease in entero-insular axis due to underlying digestive disease are risk factors for glucose metabolism impairment. We observed hyperglycaemia during PN infusion in 2 children on LTPN, suggesting insulin secretion deficiency. Our aim was to study insulin secretion and sensitivity in children on LTPN. Nine children on LTPN (age: 6-18 y) with normal glucose tolerance have been included. 1) the early phase of insulin secretion was assessed by IV glucose tolerance test (HVGGT). 2) the late phase of insulin secretion was assessed by step-by-step glucose infusion followed by arginine infusion. 3) insulin sensitivity was assessed by hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp. Out of 9 patients, 3 girls (6,13 and 18 year-old) presented with a drop of the early phase of insulin secretion (peak< 50 mUI /L) associated in 1 girl with impairment of the maximum insulin secretion. Such abnormalities, usually observed in pre-diabetic subjects, suggest that LTPN is a risk factor for the development of diabetes in children and young adults, especially in patients who remain dependent on PN.

title: DIETARY ADVICE OR EXERCISE? ‐ A LONG TERM, RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED CROSSOVER TRIAL IN A COHORT OF 10‐14 YEARS OLD GERMAN CHILDREN
abstract: Long term weight reduction programs for obese children are scarce. Therefore we performed a 12 months, randomized, controlled cross-over study to investigate the effect of dietary counselling (DC) with requested exercises (RE) vs. dietary counselling with structured exercises (SE) twice a week and its influence on body weight and body composition. 107 obese patients (female = 47; between 10 - 14 years old and BMI > 97th percentile) randomized in two groups: Group 1: DC + SE, Group 2 DC + RE for the first 6 months. The next 6 month: Group 1: DC + RE, Group 2 DC + SE. Body composition was assessed by using multifrequency bioelectric impedance (Data Input, Germany). 68 patients finished our program. Group 1: n = 39 (female = 16); Group 2: n = 29 (female = 14). BMI, BMI-SDS and FM decreased significantly in both groups. No significant differences were seen at any time in between group 1 and group 2. 58.9 % of mothers were in full-time employment and 41 children came from one parent families. For the latter drop out figure was highest (53.7 % vs. 23.5 %). Changes in dietary habits and lifestyle changes might have a stronger influence on weight reduction than exercises. Chances for prevention and early therapeutic intervention might be full-time schools integrating nutritional education and exercise programs, especially for disadvantaged children.

title: A NEW DISEASE SPECIFIC HEALTH‐RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE QUESTIONNAIRE FOR CHILDREN WITH COELIAC DISEASE: THE CDDUX
abstract: We assessed before the health-related quality of life (HRQOL) of children with coeliac disease (CD) using a CD specific questionnaire based on a generic top-down designed instrument, in which the child's well being is estimated by the researchers and physicians (1). To develop an improved bottom up designed CD specific HRQOL questionnaire for children aged 8-18 years. Development. The Dutch Celiac Patients Society (DCPS) invited at random 37 of their members aged 8-18 to participate: 70% accepted. We used a focus group method (bottom up approach) to study the impact of CD in every day life of the children and selected 24 items. The psychometric performance was statistical tested by Cronbach's alpha, factor analysis, Pearson's correlation, Student's T test, paired samples T test and Item Response Theory. Validation. The new questionnaire, together with the generic QOL questionnaire DUX 25, was sent to all 756 CD children 8-18 years members of the DCPS and was returned by 530. We compared the scores of the new questionnaire with their health status. The scores on the DUX 25 and the new questionnaire were coded into a scale from 1-100 (1 = very bad; 100 = very good). It was possible to reduced the questionnaire to12 items to construct the CDDUX, with 3 subscales: communication, diet and gluten. Children with a better health status had a better score on the CDDUX. (* = P < 0.05). The CDDUX is valid, feasible and able to discriminate the severity of the illness. Children reported a bad to neutral HRQOL. This new questionnaire may enable researchers and clinicians to determine the consequences of the illness and the effects of clinical interventions on several aspects of the daily life of children with CD. title: COMPARISON OF THE EFFECT OF CORNSTARCH THICKENED FORMULA AND STRENGTHENED REGULAR FORMULA ON REGURGITATION, GASTRIC EMPTYING AND NUTRITIONAL STATUS IN INFANTILE REGURGITATION
abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of cornstarch-supplemented formula on clinical symptoms, gastric emptying and nutritional status in infants with regurgitation. We performed a prospective randomised trial evaluating the therapeutic efficacy of two different formula feedings (cornstarch-thickened formula, group A; 25 % strengthened formula, group B) in 81 young infants with regurgitation/vomiting ≥ 3 times/day. A Tc-99m milk scintigraphy was performed at inclusion and after 2 months to quantify the number of reflux episodes and gastric emptying time; all studied infants underwent a 2-month period of clinical follow-up evaluating regurgitation and body weight gain. At inclusion, group A and B had a similar age and weight. After the two-month period of intervention, regurgitation and vomiting had both more decreased (both p < 0.001 at 1 and 2 month) in group A than in group B. Non-regurgitation symptoms (irritability, cough, choking, night awake) decreased (p = 0.045 at 1 month and 0.017 at 2 months) and weight increased (p<0.01 at 1 and 2 months) in group A as compared to group B. Gastric emptying improved significantly in group A as compared with group B (all p < 0.001 for T1/2, and residual volume at 60 and 90 minutes). Ingested feeding volume was significantly larger in the group receiving cornstarch-thickened formula. Cornstarch-thickened formula feeding decreases the frequency of regurgitation/vomiting, provides better body weight gain and has an accelerated gastric emptying in comparison to a 25 % strengthened regular formula in infants with regurgitation.

title: EFFECTS OF REDUCING THE PROTEIN QUANTITY AND RENAL SOLUTE LOAD OF INFANT FORMULA ON FORMULA INTAKE, GROWTH, PLASMA AMINO ACIDS AND INSULIN
abstract: To compare intake, growth and blood chemistry between a group of breast-fed infants and three groups of infants fed formulas differing in the amount and quality of protein and in potential renal solute load (PRSL). Breast-fed and formula-fed infants differ in energy and protein intake, growth rate, plasma amino acids and blood urea nitrogen (BUN). We hypothesized that these differences may be due to protein quantity/quality or PRSL (thirst). Double-blind randomized controlled trial of formula-fed (FF) infants (n=84) fed a) control formula (14 g pro/L; 20:80) (C), b) modified protein quality formula (14 g pro/L; 60:40) (MP) or c) low protein (12 g pro/L 0-2 mo, 11 g pro/L 2-5 mo; 60:40), low PRSL formula (LP). A comparison group of exclusively breast-fed (BF) infants (n=73) was included. Infants from Fairfield and Vacaville, CA were recruited at 2-4 wks of age and followed until 5 mo. Growth was monitored monthly, intake was measured at 1, 3 and 5 mo, and blood samples were drawn at 5 mo. Plasma amino acids, BUN and insulin were assayed. There were no sign differences among the FF groups in growth, formula intake or plasma insulin, so for this analysis the 3 groups were combined for comparisons with the BF group. The BF group was significantly lower than the FF groups in weight and length gain 1-5 mo, milk intake at 1, 3 and 5 mo, plasma insulin at 5 mo (42.6 ± 25.8 vs 65.4 ± 31.7 pmol/L, p=0.001) and plasma insulin-releasing amino acids at 5 mo (967 ± 178 vs 1133 ± 298 umol/L, p<0.01). Altering the amount and/or quality of protein in formula (and PRSL) to be more similar to breast milk did not significantly affect intake or growth. Intake and growth were significantly lower in BF than in FF infants, regardless of type of formula used. BF infants had lower plasma insulin and insulin-releasing amino acids than FF infants. title: OXIDATIVE STRESS, OXIDATIVE DNA DAMAGE AND DNA REPAIR CAPACITY IN CHILDREN AND ADULTS WITH CROHŃS DISEASE
abstract: Crohn's disease represents a model disease with important oxidative stress (OS) of inflammatory origin. The aim of the study was to examine the intensity of oxidative stress, degree of oxidative DNA damage and DNA repair in children and adults with Crohn's disease (CD). Following markers of OS were examined: superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione peroxidase (GPx), plasma antioxidant capacity (AOC), reduced glutathione (GSH) and malondialdehyde (MDA). DNA breaks were investigated in peripheral lymphocytes using comet assay technique (DNAsb). Lymphocyte capacity to repair damaged DNA (DNArc) was also assessed using the modified comet asssay. DNRI index expressed the relationship DNRI = DNArc/DNAsb. 17 CD children (7 girls, 10 boys, average age 14.29±SD 2.52 years, average disease duration 3 ± 1.43 years, PCDAI index 35.69±16.60) and 17 adult patients with Crohn's disease (11 women, 6 men, mean age 37±11.36 years, mean disease duration 10.53 ± 7.24 years, CDAI index 68.18±41.10). Results of pediatric and adult patients were compared with a group of healthy children and healthy control adults. Markers of oxidative stress did not differ significantly in children and adults with CD. DNAsb and DNRI in children were elevated, but not significantly. The intensity of DNA repair was significantly higher in children than in CD adults. The comparison with healthy controls showed that CD adults and children had significantly low GPx and AOC, further decreased levels of DNA damage, increased DNA repair capacity and similarly increased DNRI. This study confirmed important changes in markers of OS and brings new information about the intensity of DNA repair capacity rectifying oxidative DNA damage in CD patients. Both groups of CD patients cope with oxidative stress, particularly children, maybe due to their young organism and shorter disease duration.

title: PSEUDODOMINANT INHERITANCE OF WILSON DISEASE
abstract: The reported incidence of Wilson disease (WD) is approximately 1:30 000 giving a carrier frequency of 1:83. Therefore in the absence of consanguinity, WD is expected in the offspring of a case in only approximately 1:160 cases. Parental anxiety often leads to a request for testing offspring. The aim of the study was to examine families in which a parent and offspring were both affected. EuroWilson is a European database of WD patients diagnosed since January 2005. The database was searched for Wilsonian cases diagnosed through familial screening because of Wilson disease previously established in one of parents or uncles. Pedigrees, clinical characteristic and diagnostic tests were analyzed in the selected patients. Within the first 50 families entered, 7 patients, all female, in 5 non-consanguinous families were identified, aged 2.5, 4, 7, 6, 10, 22 and 25 years. 3 patients in 2 families were diagnosed because of WD in their fathers, and in 2 children mothers were affected. In 2 siblings an uncle (brother of the father) had Wilson disease. 6 children were asymptomatic, in 1 child tremor was observed. In 3 children mildly increased transaminase activity was found (AspAT 92, 118 and 169). A higher than expected frequency of apparent parent to child transmission of WD was noticed in the EuroWilson database, and has been examined. These data need confirmation in larger number of families, but suggest a higher than expected WD carrier incidence amongst partners of WD patients and by implication amongst the general population. We conclude that it is appropriate to offer diagnostic testing to the offspring of adult WD cases. The data suggests that genotypic frequency of WD is than phenotypic, which has implications for treatment decisions in asymptomatic cases.

title: The Effect of EPA and DHA on Skeletal Muscle Physiology and Energy Balance
abstract: Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) supplementation commonly suggested during pregnancy confers many health benefits on offspring and more recently improves fetal BAT development and induces myoblast trans-differentiation into adiopocytes through activating PPARs expression. Embryonic myoblast is a highly flexible cell showing great capacity to change its phenotype into adipocyte in response to EPA and DHA supplementation in many in vitro models. However, a little is known about the identity of derived adipocytes, whether, they change into brown or white adipocyte, and in vivo evidence is still missing. Given that the myogeneis process is initiated at the mid of gestation and fetal BAT development is formed at the late stage of pregnancy, we sought to investigate the effect of EPA and DHA supplementation on fetal muscle growth and energy regulation. To achieve our goal, the study was mapped in two patterns: three in vitro experiments, devoted to test the effect of combined and isolated EPA and DHA on C2C12 undergoing differentiation into white and brown adipocytes, and in vivo experiment devoted to investigate the effect of maternal ingestion of EPA and DHA enriched diet on muscle growth, BAT activity, lipid metabolism regulation in liver, and browning of sWAT. C2C12 cell have frequently been used as a representative model of myoblasts in preclinical trials. In vitro, Cells were induced to differentiate into white or brown adipocytes using hormonal cocktail in the absence (CON) or presence of (50 µm) EPA and (50 µm) DHA in combination or separately. The results suggested that EPA and DHA treatments potentiate the route of C2C12 trans-differentiation into white- like adipocytes with a greater potency of DHA in compared to EPA. The effect was mediated via inhibiting myogenesis and mitochondrial biogenesis processes and up-regulating the expression of WAT signature genes and impairing the aquistion of brown adipocyte phenotype. Changing genes profile was concurrent with increasing lipid droplets formation and impairing mitochondrial function. In vivo, mice were fed a diet containing (3.05%) fish oil (FA) enriched with EPA and DHA or diet devoid of fish oil (CON) throughout the entire period of gestation and lactation. The results showed partial inconsistency with in vitro trials where transient increase in myogenesis regulating genes and MHC4 without increasing muscle mass were observed in FA treated group. An increasing intramuscular fat infiltration as a result of stimulating the expression of adipogenesis regulating genes was predominant in FA treated group at day 1 and 21 post-parturition. Also, maternal EPA/ DHA intake induced up-regulation the expression of fatty acids catabolism regulating genes in liver. Stimulating BAT development and activity and browning of subcutaneous white adipose tissue were demonstrated in FA treated group in weaned mice. Taken together, EPA and DHA supplementation is associated with ectopic lipid accumulation in skeletal muscle but not on the expense of myoblasts, and it can be suggested as an excellent therapeutic option to combat childhood obesity as a result of their potential role in stimulating energy expenditure transcriptional program.

title: REDUCTION OF TISSUE TRANSGLUTAMINASE AUTOANTIBODY LEVELS BY GLUTEN‐FREE DIET IS ASSOCIATED WITH CHANGES IN SUBSETS OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD LYMPHOCYTES IN CHILDREN WITH NEWLY DIAGNOSED CELIAC DISEASE
abstract: Tissue transglutaminase (tTG) autoantibodies decline after gluten-free diet in patients with celiac disease. We tested the hypothesis that gluten-free diet induced change in tTG autoantibody levels affects subsets of peripheral blood lymphocytes. Peripheral blood was obtained from 20 children with biopsy-proven active celiac disease. Gluten-free diet was initiated and the children examined again after three and six months. tTG autoantibodies were measured in radioligand binding assays and lymphocyte subsets by flow cytometry. IgA-tTG levels at diagnosis, 2204 U/mL (median, range 113-24990), were reduced over six months to 76 U/mL (median, range 1-1261) (p < 0.001). At six months, 12/20 (60%) children had reduced their IgA-tTG levels to <100 U/mL and these children showed a decrease in B cells (mean change-3.8%, p = 0.014), CD4+T cells (mean-4.32%, p = 0.011) and CD4+T cells expressing CD25high (mean change-0.62%, p = 0.036). In contrast, the CD4+CD25highCCR4+T cell population increased during the same period (mean change 11.5%, p = 0.0036). The decline in IgA-tTG levels correlated to the decrease in B cells (r = 0.56, p = 0.01), CD4+ T cells (r = 0.66, p=0.004) as well as CD4+CD25high T cells (r = 0.59, p = 0.01). A negative correlation was found between the decline in IgA-tTG and CD4+CD25high T cells expressing CD45RO (r = −0.49, p = 0.03) and CCR4 (r = −0.54, p = 0.01). This observational study on the effect of gluten-free diet on concurrent changes of tTG autoantibodies and specific peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets showed that children who significantly reduced their tTG autoantibody levels after six months of treatment, also displayed the greatest changes in peripheral B and regulatory T cell subset. Our data suggest that flow cytometry may be a useful complement to tTG autoantibodies when studying the effects of gluten-free diet in children with celiac disease.

title: MODE OF DELIVERY DOCHEAD‐EFFECTS ON GUT MICROBIOTA AND HUMORAL IMMUNITY
abstract: To evaluate the establishment of gut microbiota in children born by vaginal versus caesarean delivery and its impact on mucosal immunity. 165 consecutive children were followed from birth, 141 (85%) born by vaginal delivery and 24 (15%) by caesarean section. Infants exposed to probiotics directly or through the mother were excluded. Enzyme-linked immunospot (ELISPOT) assay was used for indirect evaluation of mucosal immunity and fluorescence in situ hybridization of bacterial cells (FISH) for determination of the gut microbiota. At 1 month of age, the total gut bacterial cell counts were higher in vaginally delivered infants (9.9E9, 95% CI 7.9E9-1.2E10) as compared to caesarean delivered (3.1E9, 1.1E9-8.6E9) (p = 0.001). This distinction was due to the greater number of bifidobacteria in vaginally delivered infants (1.9E9, 95% CI 6.3E8-5.6E9 versus 1.5E6, 95% CI 4.1E2-5.7E9), (p = 0.001), but not the numbers of Clostridia, Lactobacilli or Bacteroides. During the first year of life, the number of total IgA-secreting cells was lower (p = 0.03) in infants born by vaginal versus caesarean delivery, possibly reflecting excessive antigen exposure across the vulnerable gut barrier resulting from inadequate development of the gut microbiota. A significant correlation between the mode of delivery, gut microbiota and mucosal immunity was detected. The mode of delivery has, via gut microbiota development, significant effects on immunological defence in the infant.

title: SERUM GHRELIN CONCENTRATION AND FASTING TIME IN INFANTS IN THE FIRST YEAR OF LIFE
abstract: The recent discovery of ghrelin has added new perspectives to the understanding of the control of food intake, energy balance, and growth. We investigated if serum ghrelin concentration may be influenced by fasting time in infants in the first year of life. We studied 91 AGA healthy term infants (52 males, 39 females) aged 1-12 months seen in our Department, without chronic or acute gastrointestinal disease. Serum ghrelin concentrations have been determined by RIA test (R-90, Mediagnost, Germany). Statistics: Pearson's correlation and multiple regression analysis (p<0.05). In the study group mean serum ghrelin concentration was 2980.82 ± 1424.89 pg/ml and mean fasting time was 240 ± 190 minutes. We have observed a positive correlation between ghrelin levels and fasting time (r=0.253; p=0.015). Considering kind of feeding a positive correlation between ghrelin levels and fasting time has been emerged in FF infants (r=0.436; p=0.017) and not in BF ones (r=0.186; p=0.167). In a multiple regression model considering infants' age and BMI as confounding factors, we have confirmed the positive correlation between ghrelin levels and fasting time in FF infants (Beta=0.001; ES=0.000; p=0.015); instead in BF infants we have observed a positive correlation between ghrelin levels and age (Beta=0.002; ES=0.000; p=0.001). title: ISOLATED PEDIATRIC LIVER TRANSPLANTATION FOR CYSTIC FIBROSIS
abstract: The aim of this study was to assess the role of liver transplantation (LTx) in patients with cystic fibrosis (CF)-related liver cirrhosis. In 1999 we established a program for isolated LTx in CF patients. Inclusion criteria were severe portal hypertension as well as absense of global pulmonary dysfunction. First results are presented here. The clinical and biochemical data of all children with CF who have received isolatad LTx at our centre, were analyzed. 12 children aged 8-18 years (median 16), 9 boys, were transplanted from 7/99 to 9/05 for liver cirrhosis secondary to CF. All of them had significant portal hypertension. 3 had recurrent life-threatening variceal hemorrhages and 6 received multiple endoscopic sclerotherapy. All patients demonstrated splenomegaly, ascites was found in 6 cases. Doppler ultrasound showed hepatofugal collaterals and splenorenal shunts in 10, as well as reduced portal venous flow < 20 cm/s in all patients. Ten children presented signs of hypersplenism (white cell count < 4000/μl, plated count < 100.000/μl). Hepatic synthetic function was only occasionally deranged, Albumin < 30g/l (n=3), cholinesterase < 4 kU/l (n=6) and clotting factor V < 55% (n=8). All patients were malnourished with a body mass index of less than 16 in 6 cases. Three received an overnight gastrostomy feeding. Colonization with Pseudomonas aeruginosa was found in 9. All but one were transplanted with duct-to-duct biliary anastomosis, however 2 required re-operation (Hepaticojejunostomy) due to bile duct necrosis. No re-transplantation was performed. Duration of perioperative intubation was 1-2 days and respiratory function was stable in all children. 1-year survival was 100%. During follow up 2 patients died 3 and 4 years after LTx due to Post-Transplant-Lymphoproliferative Disease and systemic Aspergillosis respectively. 10 patients are currently alive and in good clinical condition. Isolated LTx is a good therapeutic option in young patients with CF, lacking severe pulmonary disease and presenting with end-stage liver disease. Long-term survival is comparable to LTx due to other indications.

title: EFFECTS OF ALFA‐LACTALBUMIN‐ENRICHED INFANT FORMULA ON INFANT GROWTH AND NUTRITION
abstract: Formula-fed infants (FF) still have a different growth pattern, plasma amino acid pattern and gut microflora than breastfed infants (BF). α-lac is the major whey protein in human milk and addition of bovine α-lactalbumin (α-lac) to infant formula has been proposed to modify the plasma amino acid pattern of the recipient infant, possibly allowing a reduction in the protein content of formula, which, in turn may affect growth. Peptides formed from α-lac during digestion may also have prebiotic effects. We compared two experimental formulas enriched in α-lac, one with regular content of caseinoglycomacropeptide (CGMP) (α-LAC) and one with reduced CGMP (RCGMP; a major source of threonine), with a standard formula and exclusively BF infants. Protein content in all formulas was 13.1 g/L (1.96 g/100 kcal). 96 infants were recruited (control n=21; α-LAC n=20; RCGMP n=21; breastfed n=34). After enrollment at 6±2 weeks anthropometric measurements and interviews were performed monthly until 6 mo. Blood was taken at 4 and 6 mo. Formula intake did not differ between groups, but infants fed standard formula gained significantly more weight than BF infants, while the two groups fed α-lac-enriched infant formula did not differ from BF infants. All FF deviated from BF with regard to plasma amino acids. FF had significantly higher plasma concentrations of the essential amino acids threonine, isoleucine, valine, methionine, isoleucine, lysine and phenylalanine at 6 mo of age. Among FF, those fed RCGMP had branched-chain (insulinogenic) amino acids concentration closest to BF. Serum urea nitrogen was elevated in the formula-fed groups as compared to breastfed infants. Summary: Infants fed formulas with modefied protein composition had a growth pattern more similar to breastfed infants. All formula-fed groups had sufficient levels of essential amino acids. High plasma levels of essential amino acids indicate a possibility to further reduce the total protein content of formulas enriched in α-lac.

title: INFLAMMATION IS THE MAIN DETERMINANT OF BONE LOSS IN PEDIATRIC INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE
abstract: Low bone mineral density (BMD), considered as z-score ≤ −2, frequently complicates IBD. Studies on adults patients (pts) have identified inflammation and corticosteroids (CS) as major determinants of bone loss, but their role has not been clarified. to assess BMD in children with Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) and to investigate the specific role of inflammation and CS on bone loss. Lumbar spine areal BMD (aBMD) was measured by DEXA. Due to frequent growth delay in children with IBD, z-scores were reassessed on bone age. Volumetric estimation of BMD was then calculated (bone mineral apparent density, BMAD). Inflammmatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-10 and IL-12) were dosed in peripheral blood. Cumulative and daily dose of CS were calculated. Therapy with infliximab (IFX) was considered in CD pts. Correlations between BMAD and all variables were investigated. 56 pts with IBD (35 CD, 19 UC) were studied. Prevalence of low BMD was significantly higher analysing BMD as aBMD than as BMAD (39.3% and 14.3% respectively). Considering all children with IBD, plasma levels of TNF-alpha negatively affected BMAD (r = −0.37). In CD, such a correlation was stronger excluding pts on IFX (r = −0.49). IL-6 did not correlate with BMD in CD. In UC an inverse relationship was found between BMAD and both TNF-alpha and IL-6 (r = −0.59 and r = −0.64). No correlation was found between BMAD and IL-10 or IL-12. Mean daily dose of CS negatively affected BMD in IBD (r = −0.36) but not in CD or UC groups alone. Low BMD was also strongly correlated to duration of steroid therapy in UC pts (r = −0.55) but not in CD. Ten of 35 CD pts had been treated with IFX during the last 2 years before DEXA (group A). Twenty five children had never received IFX (group B). Group A had higher BMD than group B: BMAD Z-score was −0.2 ± 0.6 for group A and −1.3 ± 0.8 for group B. The stepwise multiple regression analysis with BMAD z-score as dependent variable and TNF-alpha plasma levels and mean PCDAI as predictors, showed a R2 = 0.48. For UC pts, IL-6 plasma levels and duration of therapy with CS were considered, and R2 was 0.98. Using BMAD we found a consistent but lower prevalence of low BMD in these pts, as it allows to avoid the overestimation previously reported with aBMD. Inflammation showed to be the main determinant of bone loss in both CD and UC, as proved by the strong relationship between BMD and TNF-α and IL-6 and by the protective effect of IFX on bone. CS were only important in UC. Further studies are running on the effect of inflammatory cytokines on the RANKL/OPG system.

title: BILIARY RECONSTRUCTIONS AND COMPLICATIONS ENCOUNTERED IN 44 LEFT LATERAL SEGMENT LIVING DONOR LIVER TRANSPLANTATIONS IN CHILDREN
abstract: Biliary complications appear to be the leading cause of postoperative complications after living donor liver transplantation (LDLT). The aim of this study is to analyze the complications, treatment modalities, and outcome of biliary anastomoses in a series of 44 left lateral segment LDLTs. In this study we sought to determine the safety of roux - y biliary reconstruction in live donor left lateral segment LDLTs. 49 living related liver transplantation were performed to 48 pts in our center, and 44 of them were left lateral segment LDLTs. Median patient age was 4.1 years (range 6 months - 12 years). Median left lateral segment volume was 242.5 gr (range 80gr-to 365gr). Graft- recipient weight ratio was to 1.87. Median follow up time was 50 months (range 7 days to 69 months). 12 of 44 pts died, resulting in an overall allograft and patient survival rate of %72.7. In biliary reconstruction, standart Roux-en Y (R-Y) anastomosis was performed in all cases. 32 grafts (66%) had a single duct for anastomosis. 15 grafts (32 %) had two bile duct orifices, and 1 grafts (2%) had tree bile duct orifices. The overall incidence of biliary anastomotic complications was 18.6 % (8/43 pts) in these series. 2 pts (4.6%) developed biliary leaks, presumably from the cut surface, and all of them healed spontaneously. 2 bilomas (4.6%) were drained percutaneously. Anastomotic strictures occured in 4 pts (9.3%). Three of anastomotic strictures had a single duct, one of them had two bile duct orifices. There was not any arterial thrombosis or stenosis detected. The biliary complication rate decreased significiantly in the last 3 years as well as the other complications due to the learning curve effect of the complex procedure. All strictures were managed by percutaneous measures initially. Restenosis occurred in 2 patients and one required surgical revision of the biliary anastomosis. Giving a reoperation rate of 2.1% for biliary problems. Only one graft and patient was lost because of biliary problems and accompanying septic complications. Our data suggest that Roux en Y anastomosis is a safe and feasible method of biliary reconstruction in pediatric left lateral segment LDLTs.

title: THE BREASTMILK'S CONTENT OF W6 AND W3 FATTY ACIDS HAS AN IMPACT ON THE QUALITY OF SPONTANEUS MOTOR AND EARLY MENTAL DEVELOPMENT OF PREMATURE INFANTS
abstract: Breast milk is generally considered the golden standard but long-term follow up studies have shown that preterm infants to greater extent have language and neurodevelopmental abnormalities. was to investigate whether essential fatty acids (EFA) in the mother's food and plasma, breast milk,and infant's plasma was related to the early motor and mental development. Fifty-two newborn premature infants (median age 34 weeks) were included. One week after delivery the mother's food was assessed with a 3 day food diary. Blood samples were collected from mothers and infants at the same time and in the infants corresponding to 40 and 44 weeks gestational age and analysed for phospholipid FA with GLC. The infants were assessed at 40 and 44 weeks with General Motor (GM) score and Bayley's Mental (BMe) and Motor (BMo) Scores at 3 months corrected age. None of the mothers consumed EFA in accordance with recommendations, and 32% had too low energy intake. No statistical association was found between mother's food intake and the infant's early development or quality in motor development. Linoleic (LA) and alpha-linoleic (ALA) acids increased significantly with age in the infants and arachidonic (AA) and eicosapentaenoic and docosahexaenoic acids showed opposite trends, but the range of concentration varied markedly both in breast milk and in mothers'and infants'plasma. The ratio w6/w3 and the ratio LA/ ALA in breast milk were negatively correlated to GM's at 40 weeks (r = −0.48, p=0.010 and r = −0.48, p = 0.011) and to BMe at 3 months (r = −0.50, p = 0.002 and. r = −0.43, p = 0.008). The ratio between mead acid (20:3w9) and AA, used as a marker for EFA deficiency, was in breast milk negatively correlated to GM at 40 weeks (r = −0.52, p = 0.005) and at 3 months (r = − 0.40, p = 0.014). The ratio w6/w3 in breast milk 1 week after delivery was significantly related to infant's motor development (GM's) at 40 weeks and at 3 months corrected age and also to the mental development (BMe) at 3 months of age. The general quality of FA in breast milk seemed to have consequences for short-term mental and motor quality development.
